findings.class: engagement-class shortfall at the row's own rear seam
findings.claim: The rear-bound warrant is an original-language formula claim about web:Isa.36.4 carried with no pointed splice, no tier label and no oshb: ref.
findings.grounds: Both the boundary_rationale ('The following verse opens the Rabshakeh's own royal-messenger speech with a fresh frame formula') and the strongest_rejected_alternative ('the royal-messenger formula there opens a fresh speech-frame') rest this row's rear bound on a Hebrew formula. The formula does stand in the bytes — כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר (oshb:Isa.36.4, tier: byte) — and it is one of the book's exactly four royal-messenger koh-amar sites (36:4, 36:14, 36:16, 37:3) against forty-four divine-frame verses, so the seam is materially right; but the row cites only web:Isa.36.4 and splices nothing, while the sibling row covering that verse splices the same formula at byte tier. Pointed splices plus tier labels are mandatory for every boundary-relevant original-language claim, and this is the only original-language ground the rear seam has.
findings.proposed_change: In boundary_rationale, replace 'with a fresh frame formula' with the pointed splice and tier label — 'כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר (oshb:Isa.36.4, tier: byte)' — and add 'oshb:Isa.36.4' to boundary_evidence_refs. Span unchanged.

findings.claim: An in-span paseq site is undisclosed while a sibling row in the same part discloses its own in-span paseq.
findings.grounds: oshb:Isa.36.2 carries one paseq seg in the single-witness inventory and sits inside this row's own span Isa.36.1-Isa.36.3 (chs 36-39 are identity numbering, so the MT key is the WEB key). The row discloses the parashah layer (oshb:Isa.35.10, PE, single-witness) but no paseq. Six in-span paseq verses across this batch are undisclosed (MT 36:2, 37:2, 37:4, 37:6, 37:11, 37:17 — seven segs) while MT 37:24 is disclosed in another row of the same part; symmetry completion is a sweep, not a spot fix. Paseq is count-only, never a driver, so nothing in the bound moves.
findings.proposed_change: Add a device_notes clause: 'A paseq segment is disclosed at oshb:Isa.36.2 (single-witness, a bare count lacking position data).' Span unchanged.

findings.claim: The 52-verse amar/vayomer-plus-YHWH adjacency census is invoked at web:Isa.36.10 without disclosing that the census object is order-bound, so the row's own quoted bytes appear to contradict the digit it cites.
findings.grounds: The row quotes יְהוָה֙ אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Isa.36.10, tier: byte) and then states the verse is absent from the adjacency census. The absence is true against the staged census (its 52 verses run 1:11 ... 37:6, 37:21, 37:33, 38:1, 38:5, 39:6 ... and do not include 36:10), but it is an artefact of TOKEN ORDER: the census counts amar/yomar/vayomer followed by YHWH, whereas 36:10 carries YHWH followed by amar. The row places the digit beside a speech-role argument ('the herald's own claim rather than a narrated speech event'), which the order-bound digit cannot support, and never names the ordering that produces the absence. Semantic-class count discipline requires the swept object to be named before the digit does work.
findings.proposed_change: In boundary_rationale, qualify the census clause, e.g. 'the verse is absent from the book's amar/vayomer-plus-YHWH adjacency census (52 verses), whose object is the amar-then-YHWH order and not the reversed adjacency this verse carries'. No digit change. Span unchanged.

findings.class: front-seam warrant rests on a thematic ground and disclaims the tier-1 signal in its own onset bytes
findings.claim: The row's own onset verse carries no pointed splice, no tier label and no oshb: ref, and the rationale explicitly rests the seam on an audience question 'rather than on a new speech frame' although web:Isa.36.11 opens with exactly such a frame.
findings.grounds: oshb:Isa.36.11 opens וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶלְיָקִים֩ וְשֶׁבְנָ֨א וְיוֹאָ֜ח אֶל רַב שָׁקֵ֗ה (oshb:Isa.36.11, tier: byte) — a verse-initial vayomer with a full speaker-and-addressee inversion (the three officials now speak, the Rabshakeh is now addressed), the ruled tier-1 addressee/scene-shift signal for this seam. The row instead argues 'This short unit turns on an audience question rather than on a new speech frame', quotes only WEB for that verse, splices Hebrew only at oshb:Isa.36.12, and lists no oshb:Isa.36.11 in boundary_evidence_refs. The adopted bound is materially right; the stated warrant is weaker than, and contradicts, the row's own onset bytes. Everything else re-swept in this row holds: the bare hiriq-pointed adonai census is exactly three verses (word-bound sweep of the pointed forms at MT 36:8, 36:9, 36:12), the two adonai-family forms in 36:12 are distinct at byte and at finals-normalized skeleton tier, and the doubled ketiv/qere at 36:12 matches the single-witness inventory (two notes).
findings.proposed_change: In boundary_rationale, replace 'turns on an audience question rather than on a new speech frame' with a byte-grounded onset warrant — the verse-initial speech frame with speaker-and-addressee inversion, spliced as 'וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶלְיָקִים֩ וְשֶׁבְנָ֨א וְיוֹאָ֜ח אֶל רַב שָׁקֵ֗ה (oshb:Isa.36.11, tier: byte)' — keeping the audience question as the scene rationale, and add 'oshb:Isa.36.11' to boundary_evidence_refs. Span unchanged.

findings.class: language label neither witness carries, contradicted inside the row
findings.claim: literature_type_guess calls this 'the Rabshakeh's public Hebrew proclamation' while the row's own boundary_rationale states that neither witness labels the proclamation 'Hebrew'.
findings.grounds: The verse's own noun is יְהוּדִ֑ית (oshb:Isa.36.13, tier: byte), the Judahite-language noun, and WEB reads 'in the Jews' language' (web:Isa.36.13); the row itself writes 'neither witness labels this proclamation Hebrew' and then applies the label in its own type field. The book carries no Aramaic zone (all morph codes H-prefixed), so 'Hebrew' is not false about the verse's language — it is false as a claim about what either witness calls this proclamation, which is precisely what the row's own disclosure denies. The Aramaic-label guard does not reach a Hebrew label, so the contradiction shipped unflagged.
findings.proposed_change: Rewrite literature_type_guess to the witness wording, e.g. 'the Rabshakeh's public proclamation in the Judahite language to the people on the wall, a renewed royal-messenger taunt'. Span unchanged.

findings.class: rear seam carries no byte-level warrant on either side
findings.claim: The Isa.36.20|Isa.36.21 bound is argued only from narrated content in the WEB rendering, with no ref, no splice and no boundary_evidence_refs entry for the following verse.
findings.grounds: The rationale closes 'before the officials' silence closes the scene in the following unit' — the following verse is never named, never cited and never spliced; boundary_evidence_refs stops at web:Isa.36.20 / oshb:Isa.36.16. The bound is materially right, because oshb:Isa.36.21 opens וַֽיַּחֲרִ֔ישׁוּ (oshb:Isa.36.21, tier: byte), a verse-initial wayyiqtol switching the acting subject to the officials — but that signal appears nowhere in the row, and the bare content mention carries no numeral, so the refs-mirror arm could not see it either. The neighbour row opening at 36:21 likewise argues that verse from WEB content alone, so the seam has no pointed ground on either side.
findings.proposed_change: In boundary_rationale, name the following verse and its onset — 'וַֽיַּחֲרִ֔ישׁוּ (oshb:Isa.36.21, tier: byte)', the verse-initial subject switch to the officials — and add 'web:Isa.36.21' and 'oshb:Isa.36.21' to boundary_evidence_refs. Span unchanged.

findings.class: tier-disclosure standard (recurrence claimed at 'exact token match' where only skeleton tier holds)
findings.claim: 'Verse-initial wayehi at exact token match, stands at seven verses book-wide' is tier-false: the seven-verse digit holds only at skeleton tier, and the four sites the row names carry four different byte forms.
findings.grounds: Verse-initial wayehi at skeleton tier is exactly seven verses book-wide (MT 7:1, 22:7, 36:1, 37:1, 37:38, 38:4, 48:19), so the digit is right — but at byte tier those seven split into six distinct forms, and the four sites the row lists are byte-distinct from one another: וַיְהִ֡י (oshb:Isa.36.1), וַיְהִ֗י (oshb:Isa.37.1), וַיְהִי֩ (oshb:Isa.37.38) and וַֽיְהִי֙ (oshb:Isa.38.4), all tier: byte. The 38:4 form is also distinct at accent_stripped tier, which retains meteg. The row labels every adjacent splice 'tier: byte' and names no tier for this digit, so 'exact token match' reads as a byte claim it cannot carry. The seam itself does not move: the wayehi-plus-temporal-infinitive clause with an explicit new subject stands in 37:1's own bytes.
findings.proposed_change: In boundary_rationale, replace 'at exact token match' with the honest tier — 'at finals-normalized skeleton tier (the four narrative-zone forms differ at byte tier, and oshb:Isa.38.4 differs at accent-stripped tier as well)'. Digit unchanged. Span unchanged.

findings.class: universal claim false at the scope its adjacent digit names
findings.claim: 'Only oshb:Isa.36.1 and this verse pair it with both a temporal frame and an explicit new subject' is scope-ambiguous, and false at the book scope carried by the adjacent '(sweep: 7 verses)' digit.
findings.grounds: oshb:Isa.7.1 opens וַיְהִ֡י (oshb:Isa.7.1, tier: byte) with the temporal frame בִּימֵ֣י אָ֠חָז (oshb:Isa.7.1, tier: byte) and the explicit new subject עָלָ֣ה רְצִ֣ין (oshb:Isa.7.1, tier: byte) — verse-initial wayehi paired with BOTH conditions, and the book's closest structural parallel to 36:1's own campaign-onset frame. The exclusivity is true only if silently restricted to the four narrative-zone sites, but the only digit adjacent to it is the book-wide seven, which is the scope the universal-claim rule attaches. As shipped, a reader takes the pairing as unique in the book, which the bytes deny.
findings.proposed_change: In boundary_rationale, scope the universal explicitly — 'and of those four zone sites only oshb:Isa.36.1 and this verse pair it with both a temporal frame and an explicit new subject (the same pairing also stands outside the zone at oshb:Isa.7.1)'. Add 'oshb:Isa.7.1' to boundary_evidence_refs. Span unchanged.

findings.class: false positional cross-row claim in barred register, self-contradicted in the same field
findings.claim: device_notes locates oshb:Isa.37.21 'two units later' when it opens the immediately following unit, and the same field calls it 'the following unit' one sentence earlier.
findings.grounds: This row's span closes at Isa.37.20 and the next unit runs Isa.37.21-Isa.37.35, so the prayer verb's reactivation inside that unit's divine frame sits ONE unit later, not two. The field's own first sentence already says 'distinct from the answering oracle that opens the following unit', so the two statements about the same material contradict each other. The phrase is additionally a positional row reference, which the register purge bars: cross-row references are verse-anchored. The root-tier disclosure itself is correct and no bound moves.
findings.proposed_change: In device_notes, replace 'two units later' with the verse-anchored form, e.g. 'inside the divine frame that opens at oshb:Isa.37.21'. Span unchanged.

findings.class: WEB English run attributed to the MT witness, outside the verbatim gate's window
findings.claim: A curly-quoted WEB English run is cited twice to oshb:Isa.37.35 with no web: ref anywhere near it in that field, so WEB text is attributed to the Hebrew witness and the run escapes the mandated verbatim check.
findings.grounds: In boundary_rationale the run '(curly-quoted) For I will defend this city to save it, for my own sake, and for my servant David's sake' is introduced as 'closes the unit at oshb:Isa.37.35' and followed by '(oshb:Isa.37.35)'. Curly quotes are reserved for WEB text and require an inline web: ref in the SAME field; the nearest web: ref in this field is web:Isa.37.21, 278 characters away, and the verbatim gate only scans curly runs within 200 characters of a web: ref. It is the only one of the thirty-four curly English runs across this batch that falls outside that window. The English is verbatim WEB 37:35, and web:Isa.37.35 is already in boundary_evidence_refs, so this is an attribution and disclosure repair, not a content correction. The Hebrew splice וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י עַל הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את (oshb:Isa.37.35, tier: byte) that follows is correctly attributed.
findings.proposed_change: In boundary_rationale, change both attributions around the English run from 'oshb:Isa.37.35' to 'web:Isa.37.35', leaving the separate Hebrew splice cited to oshb:Isa.37.35 at byte tier. Span unchanged.

findings.claim: device_notes locates oshb:Isa.38.6 'two units later' rather than anchoring the cross-row reference to its verse alone.
findings.grounds: The register purge bars positional row references and requires cross-row references to be verse-anchored. The position is factually consistent here — this row closes at Isa.37.35, the next unit runs Isa.37.36-Isa.37.38, and oshb:Isa.38.6 lies beyond it — and the skeleton-tier disclosure attached to it is correct: the defend-this-city clause recurs at finals-normalized skeleton tier, not byte-identically, since the accents differ between oshb:Isa.37.35 and oshb:Isa.38.6.
findings.proposed_change: In device_notes, replace 'two units later inside the healing narrative' with a verse-anchored form, e.g. 'again at oshb:Isa.38.6, inside the healing narrative'. Span unchanged.

findings.claim: 'The WEB layout carries no poetry-line markers across this song' is a span-scope universal negative with no adjacent digit-bearing sweep citation.
findings.grounds: The claim itself verifies true: every WEB verse from 37:21 to 37:35 records zero opening poetry lines, and the narrative-zone profile records 0 of 38 verses opening poetry in WEB ch 37. The campaign rule attaches a digit-bearing sweep citation naming the swept object and unit to every universal claim, and none stands beside this one. The layer is correctly declared tier-4 and expressly excluded from evidentiary use, so nothing load-bearing depends on it.
findings.proposed_change: Add the sanctioned shorthand beside the claim, e.g. 'the WEB layout carries no poetry-line markers across this song (sweep: 0 of 15 verses in this span opening a poetry line; 0 of 38 in WEB ch 37)'. Span unchanged.
